correctness.rationale: The repaired claim is the simple-promise theorem in repairs/4/RESULT.md, with the upper bound for perfect inputs clearly identified as known. A perfect target has linearly independent basis squares, so multiplying distinct images shows disjoint column support and forces the isomorphism to be monomial. The exact coefficient equation is a_ij s_j = s_i^2 b_{σ(i),σ(j)}. The directed generator cycles encode exactly the index permutations and scalar shifts, including singleton cycles for q=2; the second relation encodes that equation, including zeros and loops. Incidence paths with oriented endpoint colors preserve loops and both arc relations, and distinct pendant-leaf counts at least two recover all vertex colors. The upper reduction applies to the simple subclass because E² is a nonzero ideal in a simple algebra. For the lower bound, the unique added hub recovers n and the original nonisolated induced subgraph, and the omitted isolate count is n minus its order. The block matrix has zero kernel over every field by eliminating its two blocks in order; the bidirectional arcs make it strongly connected, so multiplication by successive natural basis vectors propagates any nonzero ideal to all squares. Over any field monomiality preserves loops and hence the x-layer, whose off-diagonal arcs recover the connected input graph; forward isomorphisms preserve both layers. The dimension is 4n+6 for n>=1, and the separate one-dimensional simple algebra handles the empty graph. The inspected frozen checker and output provide only bounded corroboration, including 2565 upper comparisons and 75 lower cases; no scripts were executed.

evidence: The survey treats rigidity, simple implies perfect, and automorphism realization, and frames the perfect finite-field complexity comparison as Question 50. Elduque–Labra give graph/automorphism structure. The isotopism graph uses pairs of elements of the full algebra.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These results do not give an all-characteristic lower gadget promised algebraically simple; embedding the simple problem into the perfect one gives the upper bound, not hardness.

evidence: In Costoya et al. b_v²=b_v and mixed natural-basis products vanish, so K b_v is a nonzero proper ideal for images of dimension greater than one. The indexed perfect hardness proof does not enforce the simple promise.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known hardness on a larger promise class does not imply hardness on the nested simple class. The repaired block construction enforces strong connectivity as well as invertibility, while looped vertices still recover the graph and the forward isomorphism remains a permutation.

evidence: Regular in Costoya et al. means E²=E, hence perfect here. Their Lemma 3.6 reflects isomorphism of pairs, not merely automorphism groups. Resultary 58409c6864d5 states fixed-field GI-completeness for perfect inputs with a two-relation graph on n(q−1) vertices.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The original perfect-case headline is covered even if presentations of the lower gadget differ; simple in the repaired claim means absence of nonzero proper ideals, not regularity.

evidence: The closest catalogue theorem covers the perfect-domain result and upper graph size; it gives a perfect block-unitriangular lower gadget rather than the simple-promise statement.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Exact finite isomorphism class tables cannot settle this unbounded reduction theorem. The matching indexed theorem, not the finite checker, supplies exact coverage of the perfect domain.

originality.rationale: The original perfect-promise contribution fails originality: a distinct earlier Resultary result already gives both fixed-field reductions (including the n(q−1)-vertex upper reduction), and Costoya et al. prove perfect-algebra hardness with an explicit isomorphism-reflecting construction over all fields. The repair claims as contribution only the faithful all-characteristic simple-algebra lower construction and the consequent complexity result on that stronger promise. This is distinct in the inspected comparisons: Costoya et al.'s vertex lines are already nonzero proper ideals when the dimension exceeds one. The upper reduction and known structural facts are credited and reused, not claimed as contributions.
residual_risks: The bounded comparisons do not certify historical priority or exclude an unlocated graph-to-simple-algebra reduction or an equivalent construction in different terminology.

value.rationale: Hardness after imposing algebraic simplicity is a meaningful strengthening: direct regular-algebra encodings need not satisfy it. The linear-dimension, 0–1 construction keeps rigidity and graph recovery while supplying simplicity uniformly in the characteristic. This isolates which structural restriction does not lower the complexity, rather than restating the known perfect-case classification.
